subject: Re: Docs-a-thon: request for platform credits & trial extension
messages:
From: Linus Park <linus@opendocs.org>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Docs-a-thon: can Redwood help with platform credits?

Hi Rishi,

Hope you’re well — I run community operations at OpenDocs Collective. We’re organizing a 48-hour Docs-a-thon (Oct 10–12) focused on improving docs, guides, and tutorials across OSS projects. We had great turnout last year and want to offer maintainers lightweight access to model-backed authoring workflows during the event.

Two asks:
- Do you have promo credits or trial extensions we can offer maintainers so they can experiment with Redwood’s developer tooling?
- Any chance for a short keynote/demo (15–20min) to show how teams can use your platform for docs automation?

We’re a small non-profit; visibility for Redwood in the event program (logo, mention in the opening remarks, featured in the sponsor email) would be the only expectation in return.

Would love to understand what’s feasible (amount of credits, expiration, any usage limits).

Thanks — Linus
Linus Park
Community Ops, OpenDocs Collective
https://opendocs.org

Attachment: opendocs_docs-a-thon_brief.docx (1 page event outline)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Linus Park <linus@opendocs.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Docs-a-thon: can Redwood help with platform credits?

Hi Linus — thanks for the note and congrats on running this — sounds like a great event. Quick answers up front:

- We can offer promotional credits to individual maintainers (up to a program cap) plus a temporary trial extension for orgs that sign up.
- We’re happy to do a short keynote/demo; Marissa (cc’d) will help coordinate timing and format.

Couple of clarifying Qs before I put together a proposal:
1) How many maintainers (unique people) do you expect to enable with credits?
2) Do you prefer per-person small grants (e.g., $200-$500 equivalent credits) or a pool that projects can draw from?
3) Any compliance or DPA concerns we should be aware of for non-profit participants?

Proposal I’m thinking of (pending sign-off): 
- $2,500 in platform credits dedicated to the event, distributed as $250 vouchers to up to 10 maintainers + 30-day trial extension for accepted project teams.
- Redwood keynote (15 minutes) + 30-minute interactive Q&A/workshop.
- Sponsor callouts in the opening email and event page.

I’ll draft a sponsorship agreement once Marissa confirms budget/approval.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- Please add a short mutual action plan to the sponsorship_agreement (who issues vouchers, redemption process, expiration timeframe).
- Legal wants the standard event sponsor addendum (I attached a draft).

Vivek — can you confirm we have runway in the promo budget for this and sign off on the sponsor addendum? If finance needs a PO or SOW to release credits, flag it.

Subject: Redwood support confirmed — next steps and MAP

Hi Linus — great to confirm: Redwood is able to provide the $2,500 in platform credits for the Docs-a-thon plus organization-level 30-day trial extensions for accepted teams. Key details below: 

What we will provide:
- Credits: $2,500 total, issued as up to 10 vouchers of $250 each. Vouchers are single-use and tied to an email address.
- Trial extension: 30-day extension to the standard free trial for project teams that register via your event form.
- Redwood speaker: 15-min demo + 30-min workshop slot.
- Marketing: logo + sponsor mention in the opening email and event page.

Operational items (MAP):
1) Linus to provide list of maintainers/recipient emails (or a redemption form) by Sep 15, 2026.
2) Redwood issues vouchers within 3 business days of receiving the list or redemption confirmations.
3) Voucher expiry: 90 days from issuance.
4) Contact for redemption issues: promo-support@redwoodinference.com

Attached: sponsorship_agreement_v1.pdf (for signature). I’ll also create a short DocuSign envelope and share the link once legal approves the addendum.

Next steps for you: reply with the preferred distribution model (direct list vs open redemption form) and confirm acceptance of the MAP.

Thanks — excited to support this.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
